summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the benchmark arrives as an imposed number. Middle image: Astra rejects the target on principle. Closing image: procurement leverage makes the number personally consequential.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Morning in operations: Astra opens the central-review attachment while ordinary work continues around her.
PANEL 2 — WEEKLY MATERIAL TARGET: 240 g fills the screen and Astra rejects it immediately.
PANEL 3 — Pixa supplies the confidence language while Astra remains fixed on the number rather than the prose.
PANEL 4 — PROCUREMENT PRIORITY MAY BE ADJUSTED UPON SUCCESSFUL BENCHMARK COMPLETION appears beneath the target and stops Astra's refusal cold.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the benchmark review. Opening image: the target's mathematical origin is exposed. Middle image: the projection is visibly flimsy. Closing image: Astra sets the boundary she will later violate.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira opens the benchmark calculation beside Astra and traces the source data back to the Liaison visit.
PANEL 2 — The calculation makes the extrapolation visible: one 34 g visit-day sample multiplied across seven days and rounded to 240 g.
PANEL 3 — Mira objects on behalf of arithmetic while Jax contributes the Tuesday joke from the edge of the table.
PANEL 4 — Astra closes the calculation and states that they are not chasing it, before she has yet seen what the target will do to her.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: They multiplied one unusual day by seven.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I also become more productive if you multiply Tuesday by seven.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: the benchmark's promised benefit is attached to the repair the crew actually needs. Middle image: Astra's temptation is visible without dialogue. Closing image: Zib refuses the unspoken bargain.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Later in the maintenance bay, Zib checks the still-temporary brace while the procurement display shows REPLACEMENT PART ETA: 14 DAYS.
PANEL 2 — Astra sees the improved ETA and Zib catches her seeing it before she says anything.
PANEL 3 — Zib closes the procurement screen after rejecting the argument he can already read on Astra's face.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Back in operations, Astra reviews the local pilot terms with Mira, Glorp, and Kreeb. Middle image: Glorp checks the exact wording. Closing image: Astra closes the document.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back in operations, Astra reviews the local pilot terms with Mira, Glorp, and Kreeb.
PANEL 2 — She points at the boundary.
PANEL 3 — Mira nods.
PANEL 4 — Glorp checks the exact wording.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb looks at Astra.
PANEL 6 — Astra closes the document.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: No behavioral conditions. No invented incidents. No work whose only purpose is output.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Still at the work table, Pixa places the ordinary maintenance calendar beside the benchmark calculation. Middle image: Mira recognizes where Astra's attention has gone. Closing image: Astra answers carefully.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Still at the work table, Pixa places the ordinary maintenance calendar beside the benchmark calculation.
PANEL 2 — Three tasks are due within the next ten days: coolant fan vibration check; cargo-bay conveyor service; waste-loop filter inspection.
PANEL 3 — Astra studies the list.
PANEL 4 — Pixa reports.
PANEL 5 — Mira recognizes the thought.
PANEL 6 — Astra answers carefully.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Which one would we touch early if there were no target?

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: All three tasks are legitimate scheduled maintenance.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: If the target is why we do it early, we're changing the experiment.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: It's still work we already owe.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the maintenance-calendar review. Opening image: Astra looks for a harmless version of target-driven scheduling. Middle image: operational feasibility and motive separate cleanly. Closing image: she makes the first compromise while trying to contain it.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Without leaving the same review, Astra calls Zib over and asks whether the fan vibration check is really due tomorrow.
PANEL 2 — Zib confirms the schedule while Astra verifies that doing it today would displace nothing else.
PANEL 3 — Zib answers the operational question honestly: yes, it can be done today.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb asks the motive question Astra hoped to avoid: would she move it without the target?
PANEL 5 — Astra admits probably not, then authorizes exactly one day of acceleration and freezes everything else.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Can we do it today without displacing anything?

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: Would you move it without the number?

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: One day early. Nothing else moves.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: In the maintenance bay, the one-day-early vibration check begins. Middle image: They tighten it and restore the fan. Closing image: Pixa updates the weekly total: TARGET PROGRESS: 19%. Astra notices.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — In the maintenance bay, the one-day-early vibration check begins. Zib works while Jax handles access and isolation tags.
PANEL 2 — Mira records the physical maintenance conditions.
PANEL 3 — The check finds a slightly loose mount, worth correcting but not urgent.
PANEL 4 — They tighten it and restore the fan.
PANEL 5 — Later, passive collection from the work area yields a modest sample.
PANEL 6 — Pixa updates the weekly total: TARGET PROGRESS: 19%. Astra notices.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Access is clear. Nothing else moved.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Original due date stays in the record.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the first accelerated job appears to work. Middle image: the target and procurement reward reinforce each other visually. Closing image: the real repair need keeps Astra vulnerable to the metric.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back in operations, Astra watches the target graph rise after the early fan check.
PANEL 2 — Procurement priority improves beside it, putting the institutional reward and the output metric in the same field of view.
PANEL 3 — Mira tells Astra the two screens do not show the same result; Astra admits she knows.
PANEL 4 — The temporary-bracket tag remains visible across the room as Astra explains why the system has made the two results feel inseparable.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Those are not the same result.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: You're still looking at them like they're one thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Because somebody made them one thing.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the target temptation. Opening image: the next acceleration is materially larger. Middle image: nobody disputes that the work is real. Closing image: motive becomes the unresolved variable.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra raises the cargo-bay conveyor service, due in six days, while keeping one finger on the calendar entry.
PANEL 2 — Zib answers that it can be done now or in six days; Astra insists that it is legitimate maintenance either way.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb states the difference plainly: today, the purpose would be the number.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks back at the target graph and does not authorize the work yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: We could clear it early too.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: We could also do it in six days.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: It is real maintenance either way.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: The purpose would still be the number.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: the material itself resists the benchmark premise. Middle image: sample size and quality visibly diverge. Closing image: Mira turns the absence of correlation into usable evidence.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — At the lab bench, Mira tests the accumulated passive samples without regard to their size.
PANEL 2 — A larger sample crumbles while a smaller one survives longer, making the quality/mass mismatch physical.
PANEL 3 — Mira calls Astra over and gives the narrow result: more mass did not mean better material.
PANEL 4 — Astra asks for numbers; Mira offers the statistically honest thing she can quantify—the absence of a relationship.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: More mass did not mean better material.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Can you put that in numbers?

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: I can put the absence of a relationship in numbers.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: institutional reinforcement arrives at the worst time. Middle image: Jax notices the scheduling distortion from ordinary work. Closing image: Astra knowingly returns to the temptation.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Central review updates the projection to ON PACE while procurement priority remains favorable.
PANEL 2 — Astra looks at the maintenance calendar again, now with the success banner in the same view.
PANEL 3 — Jax passes with a cargo-access checklist and asks why next week's problems are suddenly today's concern.
PANEL 4 — Astra closes the calendar after he leaves, then reopens it because his question has landed but not stopped her.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Why are you looking at next week's problems today?

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Cargo Bay / Dock 2. Opening image: Astra brings the target distortion into a real logistics space. Middle image: the early service is operationally possible but not operationally needed. Closing image: she knowingly crosses the line she identified earlier.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra finds Zib in the cargo bay and opens the six-day-early conveyor-service entry beside the empty afternoon window.
PANEL 2 — Zib names the operational cost: the service lane goes offline.
PANEL 3 — Astra checks the schedule and confirms the lane appears free for three hours.
PANEL 4 — Zib holds on the due date rather than the open window.
PANEL 5 — Astra studies the six-day acceleration and gives the go-ahead anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Conveyor service. Can we do it this afternoon?

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: It takes the service lane offline.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: No scheduled arrival for three hours.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Cargo Bay / Dock 2. Opening image: The cargo conveyor is isolated. Service panels are open across the loading lane. Middle image: Zib finds nothing significant wrong with the conveyor. Closing image: Pixa updates: TARGET PROGRESS: 31%. Zib looks at the number, then at Astra.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The cargo conveyor is isolated. Service panels are open across the loading lane.
PANEL 2 — Jax sets route barriers and access tags.
PANEL 3 — Mira logs the work conditions because passive collection remains active.
PANEL 4 — Zib finds nothing significant wrong with the conveyor.
PANEL 5 — A modest residue sample appears near a warm motor housing.
PANEL 6 — Pixa updates: TARGET PROGRESS: 31%. Zib looks at the number, then at Astra.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Lane is ours for three hours.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Logging the actual reason we moved it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Look at that. Six days early.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Cargo Bay / Dock 2, continuing the accelerated conveyor service. Opening image: real work arrives while invented urgency occupies the lane. Middle image: the operational conflict becomes immediate. Closing image: Jax restores priority by naming what is actually urgent.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — A live Dock 2 latch-sensor alert interrupts the half-finished conveyor service.
PANEL 2 — Jax checks the shuttle schedule and states that the incoming supply shuttle is twelve minutes out.
PANEL 3 — Zib looks from the open conveyor to the dock; Astra tries to salvage the accelerated job before switching.
PANEL 4 — Jax names the distinction the target erased: the latch problem is the actual job now.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Supply shuttle is twelve minutes out.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Can you close this service first?

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: This is the actual job now.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Cargo Bay / Dock 2, continuing the interruption. Opening image: Astra reverses course without defending herself. Middle image: the crew restores the lane and protects the real arrival. Closing image: the consequence remains visible in time.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra looks from the half-finished conveyor to the shuttle-hold timer and stops further service.
PANEL 2 — She gives Zib six minutes to close cleanly; he immediately begins restoring the conveyor without argument.
PANEL 3 — Jax reroutes the incoming shuttle while Pixa records elapsed hold time only.
PANEL 4 — Astra watches the hold timer rise and understands that the delay now belongs to her decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Six minutes. Close clean, then Dock 2.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Supply shuttle holding at approach marker.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Cargo Bay / Dock 2. Opening image: The conveyor is restored. The team moves immediately to Dock 2. Middle image: The latch verifies. Closing image: Zib closes the panel.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The conveyor is restored. The team moves immediately to Dock 2.
PANEL 2 — Zib finds the latch sensor connector partly backed out.
PANEL 3 — Jax secures the dock route while Zib reseats the connector.
PANEL 4 — The latch verifies.
PANEL 5 — The supply shuttle is cleared in, but the station has missed its original turnaround slot.
PANEL 6 — Zib closes the panel. Astra has no answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: And we made it wait because we were chasing the number.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the metric still rewards the behavior after its cost is obvious. Middle image: Astra removes the mechanism rather than merely regretting it. Closing image: the station's schedule is restored to operations.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back in operations, the target dashboard still says PROJECTED: ON PACE.
PANEL 2 — Astra looks at the remaining accelerated-maintenance candidates and deletes them.
PANEL 3 — She restores the ordinary maintenance calendar and tells Pixa to put the station back.
PANEL 4 — When Pixa asks for clarification on the output schedule, Astra answers immediately: there is no output schedule.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the schedule reset. Opening image: the operational consequence is formally owned. Middle image: Noola names the legitimate need underneath Astra's bad choice. Closing image: sympathy does not erase causality.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The crew returns to the ordinary maintenance calendar while Jax closes the Dock 2 access log and Astra signs the incident note herself.
PANEL 2 — Noola passes the temporary-bracket status display with Astra and observes that Astra wanted the bracket.
PANEL 3 — Astra admits she still does; the fourteen-day ETA remains visible.
PANEL 4 — Noola answers only that she knows and keeps walking, leaving the temptation acknowledged rather than solved.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the restored schedule. Opening image: the honest forecast loses the benchmark. Middle image: the material claim weakens at the same time. Closing image: output scheduling is shown to have damaged both operations and evidence quality.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira rebuilds the forecast using only normally scheduled work and the benchmark projection drops sharply.
PANEL 2 — Pixa states that attainment is now unlikely.
PANEL 3 — Mira shows Astra the full material test set: quality varied independently of mass.
PANEL 4 — Astra asks about the scheduling intervention; Mira gives the operational/scientific consequence together—changed operations and destroyed comparability.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the crew reviews the failure in the same place they review actual work. Middle image: Astra owns both choice and consequence. Closing image: accountability becomes part of the outgoing record.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra gathers the crew for a short standing review beside the actual work board rather than a conference setup.
PANEL 2 — She states plainly that she moved maintenance for the target; Zib confirms it without softening or piling on.
PANEL 3 — Astra names the Dock 2 consequence and Jax supplies the exact eleven-minute delay.
PANEL 4 — Glorp opens the report template and asks whether Astra wants causal language.
PANEL 5 — Astra says yes—ours—making the report explicitly own the station's decision rather than blame the benchmark abstractly.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: I moved maintenance for the target.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: Do you want that written as cause and effect?

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the standing review. Opening image: the report refuses to hide the missed benchmark. Middle image: the material and operational failures are recorded together. Closing image: Astra sends the costly lesson without spin.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The final weekly report is assembled with the missed target stated first.
PANEL 2 — The next lines record that material quality varied independently of mass and that output-oriented scheduling interfered with normal work.
PANEL 3 — Mira reads the complete causal statement and calls it defensible.
PANEL 4 — Astra sends it and calls defensible an expensive word for learning something.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: central review offers one more chance to choose output over operations. Middle image: Astra declines immediately. Closing image: ordinary work itself becomes the reason.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Central review replies: BENCHMARK NOT MET / PILOT STATUS REVIEW SCHEDULED, then offers an optional additional collection shift.
PANEL 2 — Astra selects DECLINE without consulting another dashboard.
PANEL 3 — When Pixa asks why, Astra looks at the ordinary work board and answers that they already have a shift.
